thread:
neal: quick heads-up from today's microbench — tiny requests (<=32 tokens) p50 jumped after yesterday's kernel change. total p50 14.0ms -> host_parse 7.6ms, kernel_dispatch 3.4ms, decode 3.0ms

neal: digging in: host_parse breakdown shows tokenization 4.6ms, grpc/http2 frame handling 1.1ms, writev coalesce debounce 1.9ms, plus ~0.6ms sync KV prefetch on hits

priya: that tokenization number seems large for a 2-3 token payload. did the new kernel change the input packing?

neal: yes — kernel X path adds a wide->narrow copy when attaching KV metadata. small-request fast-path still goes through full parse, so we pay the extra memcpy.

jack: interesting. two levers: (A) avoid the copy (stream tokenization straight into the outbound buffer for small reqs) (B) prefer kernel Y for <64 tokens to skip the wide->narrow path, or bump minibatch window so host can coalesce before packing

maria: I'll run a canary with early writev coalescing + async KV prefetch and a runtime flag to prefer kernel Y for small requests. jack, can you add host_preparse.minibatch_ms=6 and host_preparse.pref_kernel=Y for the canary?

jack: will do. also adding a telemetry counter for tokenization time and KV-prefetch sync vs async hits/misses.

priya: load-test reminder — we must validate throughput under high concurrency if we change batching window. Tokenization-only wins are great but not if they cause tail regressions for bursty workloads.

maria: load tests queued. will post perf + tail numbers in ~90m. tagging @sre_bot to create canary watch.

sre_bot: canary watch created: id=canary-6480012345, alert_on_tail_increase=50% over baseline, duration=15m

neal: tentative rollout plan: (1) ship writev coalesce + async kvcache prefetch if canary stable (2) follow-up ticket to refactor tokenization pipeline for in-place streaming into outbound buffers (3) audit kernel-selection heuristics for tiny-request fast-path

priya: thanks everyone. small host-side fixes move the needle for PLG latency — appreciate quick turnaround. :rocket:
